quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you?

options.text: It makes you feel falsely confident.

questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. It can make you feel overly confident or silly. Alcohol also slows your reaction time, coordination, and balance. It affects your vision and ability to judge distance, making it hard to react quickly.

questions.question: Which substances can impair your driving and lead to a DUII arrest?
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. These include all alcoholic drinks, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medications such as prescription and over-the-counter drugs.

questions.question: What should you do if you are in a serious car crash?
questions.explanation: If you crash, move your vehicle off the road and stop if you can. If anyone is hurt, call 911 and help them. You must report the crash to police if someone is injured, someone dies, or if there is more than $1,000 in property damage (or more than $200 in damage to government property like signs or guardrails).

questions.question: License plates must be:

options.text: Secured so they do not swing.
Clean and easy to read at all times.

questions.explanation: License plates must be mounted flat at least 12 inches from the ground and fastened so they do not swing. They must be clearly visible and kept clean and readable.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal your intention ahead of time, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before you move.

questions.question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is true?

options.text: Never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
Airbags can hurt an infant or small child, even in a low-speed crash.
Make sure all passengers use a seat belt or child restraint.

questions.explanation: Before driving, fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts greatly reduce your chances of being hurt or killed in a crash. Children 12 and under must sit properly restrained in a back seat. Never put a rear-facing infant seat in the front seat of a vehicle with a front airbag.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Stay calm and move out of their way.
Flash your lights to show the driver they are wrong.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm and move out of their way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, stay calm and get away from them. Trying to get even with an aggressive driver can make the situation more dangerous.

questions.question: What is the best way to reduce your risk of injury or death in a car crash?

options.text: Stay in the right lane on multilane highways.
Only drive between 3:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m.

questions.explanation: Wearing your seat belt is the single most effective way to reduce your risk of death or injury while driving.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Make turns more slowly than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast on slippery roads is always dangerous, especially in turns and curves. Approach turns more slowly in slippery conditions than you would normally.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Slow down and yield for trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield for trains.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that railroad tracks are ahead. Slow down when approaching railroad crossings. Trains cannot stop for cars, so you must wait for the train to pass before crossing the tracks.

questions.question: What does alcohol do?

options.text: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain and makes it harder to drive safely. It reduces your reaction time and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: You had an upsetting incident at work and feel angry. When you get to your car, what should you do?

options.text: Play the radio loudly to distract yourself.
Drive fast on the interstate to release stress.
Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Stop at a bar and drink before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, wait until you feel calm before driving. Driving while emotional is dangerous to you and others on the road.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing and do not see or hear a train. When must you stop?

options.text: If a stop sign is posted.
If a crossing gate is lowered.
If the crossing lights are flashing red.

questions.explanation: Always stop before a railroad crossing if red lights are flashing, a gate is lowered, a stop sign is posted, or a person signals you to stop. Never try to cross ahead of a train.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When a person signals you to stop.
When a stop sign is there.
When red flashing lights and gates are working.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a person signals you, when there is a stop sign, and when red flashing lights and gates are working.

questions.question: Another driver cuts you off in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Pull up next to them and yell.
Let it go and move on.
Flash your high beams at them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let it go and move on.
questions.explanation: Do not take it personally when another driver cuts you off. Let it go and continue driving safely to avoid road rage.

questions.question: An aggressive driver is following you closely. What should you do?

options.text: Stare at the driver as they pass.
Speed up while they are passing.

questions.explanation: Get out of an aggressive driver's way. Do not make eye contact with them. Speeding up may make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: What is true about drivers who have consumed alcohol?

options.text: They are always aware of the risks they take.
They cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
They are better drivers because they are more careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol hurts your judgment, vision, focus, and reaction time. Never drink any amount of alcohol before driving.

questions.question: Why should you not follow other cars too closely?

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car in front stops suddenly.
You may not see their turn signals.
You may not see their brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car in front stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: Following too closely means you cannot stop in time if the car ahead stops suddenly. This causes collisions.

questions.question: When is it important to slow down?

options.text: When the road is wet or slippery.

questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections and railroad crossings, on hills, on curves you cannot see around, where there are pedestrians, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: Where is it illegal to pass another vehicle?
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills, curves, at intersections, or at railroad crossings. These are unsafe places to pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic is coming from both directions ahead.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Watch what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow traffic light means a red light is coming. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Pull to the right side of the road and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights behind you, slow down and pull safely to the right side of the road. Stop and let the emergency vehicle pass. If you are in heavy traffic and cannot move right away, keep moving slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: When you turn or change lanes, you must:

options.text: Always signal, even if you do not see other traffic.
Signal only if you see other traffic.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal, even if you do not see other traffic.
questions.explanation: Always signal when you turn, change lanes, or pull away from a curb. Signaling is a law. Make it a habit every time.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer cross this road. Slow down, stay alert, and be ready to stop.
